contracts.description: The interchange format: canonical JSONL serialization, lossless round-trip, structural and closed-world-scope validation (lint), fixture hashing, and index rebuild from committed files.

VerificationRecord submission and the conformance ledger: record validation and ingestion, gating, verdict derivation including waivers and the conforms-with-waivers token, and conformance reporting. Since 3.0.0: JudgmentRecord ingestion and the graduation function — judgment-criterion gating derived from recorded judge verdicts (calibration-corpus admissibility, reproducibility tolerance, derived provenance).

The author-class protocols: promotion (ratification as a total function over spec, transition, clock), author-output validation (lint-valid, budgeted, provenance-honest), excavate-output validation (scoped, discovered+proposed), render audience projection (exact content inventories), and prime protocol emission. All criteria proposed at 1.0.0; gating begins at ratification.

exclusions: Execution: felag never runs implementations, spawns agents, or manages sessions; verify is a ledger, not a runner.
Work state: no work tables or work verbs in core; the felag-tasks contract is a sibling conformance unit.
Identity: attribution fields are free-form strings with no semantics; no trust hierarchy, no identity model.
Memory and preference content: profiles are written by people or agents from whatever they use; felag owns the profile format only.
CLI output formatting, log formats, error-message wording, latency, pagination order, and render aesthetics: observable but undeclared, therefore non-core.
Cross-person claim visibility: removed, not deferred.

felag/author residue at 1.0.0: the author --from-annotations round-trip (requires an annotation format that does not exist yet); interview conduct (a dialog, not an artifact — judgment permanently, by the same reasoning that verify is a ledger); Profile and Binding rendering (those artifacts ship with implementations; rendering them waits for their formats to become contract surface).

Judge execution: felag never calls a judge model, hosts a rubric prompt, or schedules judge runs; judgment verdicts arrive as JudgmentRecords exactly as conformance checks arrive as VerificationRecords, and the independence of judge runs is attested by the records, not verified — the runner-integrity stance applied to judging. Target verdicts are calibrated attestation, not third-party-reproducible checks: only calibration records are publicly checkable against the anchor corpus (it-judgment states the asymmetry plainly). (The judgment-gating exclusion that stood from 1.0.0 was removed at 3.0.0: the graduation bar it required — reproducibility tolerance, calibration-corpus judge substitution, verdict provenance — is it-graduation.)

Interchange residue at 2.0.0: CS6 writer refusal of finite-JSON, non-finite-double numerals is normative but unfixturable in interchange - the corpus cannot canonically carry the value whose refusal it would pin; the obligation rides on prose and implementation tests, not fixtures.
goals: Specs are authored and consumed as prose but stored as a strict, line-oriented schema; nothing in conformance depends on any model, vendor, or agent framework.
A spec is a standing contract: implementations drift, the spec is what they drift from, and the verifier measures it.
Conformance is derived from recorded evidence, never asserted bare; overrides exist only as recorded, justified, expiring waivers that are loud in every report.
The toolchain is specced in felag by conformance class, so a stranger can reimplement any class in any language and verify the mechanical classes against this spec.
name: felag-core

body:
A felag spec is committed as line-oriented JSONL under an interchange directory: spec/<name>/spec.jsonl holds one preamble record followed by item records, each item followed by its criterion records (criterion.itemId names the parent); spec/<name>/fixtures.jsonl holds fixture records. The committed interchange files are the source of truth; any database or index (Dolt or otherwise) is a regenerable local accelerator, never authoritative, never committed.

Canonical serialization rules, derived during this compilation as design v1.1 requires (the requirement is normative; these rules make it mechanical):
CS1. Encoding is UTF-8 without BOM; the line separator is LF; a file ends with exactly one trailing LF; no blank lines, no comments.
CS2. Each line is exactly one JSON object (a record) serialized with no insignificant whitespace (separators ',' and ':').
CS3. Every record carries a 'record' field naming its type: preamble | item | criterion | fixture.
CS4. Key order: 'record' first, then 'id' when present, then all remaining keys ascending by Unicode code point; keys of nested objects are ordered ascending by Unicode code point.
CS5. String escaping: only quotation mark, backslash, and control characters U+0000-U+001F are escaped; the short escapes \b \f \n \r \t are used where defined, otherwise \u00xx with lowercase hex; all other characters, including non-ASCII, are emitted literally as UTF-8. A lone surrogate - an unpaired code unit U+D800-U+DFFF - has no UTF-8 representation and is the single exception: it is escaped as \udXXX with lowercase hex, matching ECMAScript well-formed JSON.stringify and RFC 8785.
CS6. Every number field this format defines is a decimal integer; schema validation constrains these fields to integer values, and the canonical lexeme - no leading zeros, plus sign, fraction, or exponent - is a writer rule. Payload subtrees (a fixture's input and expected) are schema-opaque - ungated, never validated - but not byte-opaque: canonicalization reorders their keys (CS4), re-escapes their strings (CS5), and re-serializes their numbers. They may carry any JSON number whose IEEE-754 double value is finite: its canonical form is the ECMAScript string serialization of that double (RFC 8785 section 3.2.2.3) - integer values of magnitude below 10^21 emit as plain decimals, identical to the field lexeme; magnitudes of 10^21 and above take the ECMAScript exponential form (1e+21), and magnitudes below 10^-6 take it too (1e-7); non-integers emit shortest round-trip (600.5); negative zero emits as 0. The lexeme never survives canonicalization: 600.50 and 6.005e2 both emit as 600.5. A payload number IS its IEEE-754 double, by definition: a JSON numeral beyond double precision denotes the nearest double (round-to-nearest-even), so 9007199254740993 and 9007199254740992 are the same payload value and canonicalize identically, and underflow is the same value rule: 1e-400's nearest double is 0 and it canonicalizes silently to 0. Within the finite range, precision loss is silent by definition; only the finite/non-finite edge refuses. The interchange round-trip guarantee is value-level, canonical-form to canonical-form; source lexemes are not values (the I-JSON stance, RFC 7493). Identifiers needing more than 53 bits of integer precision travel as strings. A numeral that is valid JSON but whose double value is non-finite (1e309) has no canonical form: a conforming writer refuses to serialize the record rather than corrupt the value; readers remain liberal. The refusal is unfixturable in this interchange - the corpus cannot canonically carry the value it must refuse - and is recorded as residue in the exclusions.
CS7. Record order in spec.jsonl: preamble first, then items in author-declared order, each immediately followed by its criteria in author-declared order.
CS8. Record order in fixtures.jsonl: fixtures sorted ascending by id in code-point order.
CS9. The canonical hash of a fixture is 'sha256:' followed by the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes of its canonical record line, excluding the trailing LF.

Readers MUST accept any record set that validates against the schema regardless of serialization details (key order, whitespace, escaping); writers MUST emit canonical form. interfaceSketch on an item is optional and non-normative: it never gates and carries no conformance meaning.
title: Interchange format

gherkin:
Given a spec file in canonical interchange form
When a conforming implementation parses it and re-serializes it
Then the output bytes are identical to the input bytes

Given interchange records serialized in a non-canonical but schema-valid form
When a conforming implementation reads them and writes the spec file
Then the output is the canonical serialization (CS1-CS8) of the same records

Given committed interchange files and any local index built from them
When the index is deleted, rebuilt from the interchange files alone, and the interchange is regenerated from the rebuilt index
Then the regenerated files are byte-identical to the committed files

Given interchange records whose fixture payloads carry finite JSON numbers, integer and non-integer alike
When a conforming implementation parses any schema-valid spelling and writes canonical form
Then every number emits as the ECMAScript serialization of its IEEE-754 double value - shortest round-trip, lexeme-independent, value not lexeme - and the output round-trips byte-identically

body:
lint is the merge gate of the interchange class: schema validity, unique ids across all records, declared-contract membership, the fixture rule, and version-bump consistency. Closed-world scope is enforced structurally: the preamble's contracts are the allowlist, and a criterion referencing a contractId not declared there is invalid. A criterion with no contractId is not an error: it is advisory by construction and can never gate.

Lint result format (derived during compilation; the design defines no tool output formats): {"valid": boolean, "errors": [{"code", "ref"}]} with errors sorted ascending by (code, ref) and ref naming the offending record id. Error codes at 1.0.0: E_SCHEMA (record fails the JSON Schema), E_DUPLICATE_ID, E_UNDECLARED_CONTRACT, E_MISSING_FIXTURES, E_UNKNOWN_FIXTURE (a fixtures entry names no fixture record), and the roster checks E_DUPLICATE_IMPLEMENTER (two roster entries share a name; ref is the duplicated name) and E_MULTIPLE_OWNERS (more than one roster entry carries the repo-owner role; ref is 'preamble') - roster-reference resolution and the promotion tiebreak both presuppose them. At 3.0.0: E_BAD_TOLERANCE - a judgment object's tolerance violating 2 x agreement > runs, or carrying agreement > runs, naming the criterion (the first would let reproducible-pass and reproducible-fail hold at once; the second is unreachable - a window of runs records can never carry more than runs agreeing verdicts; the schema constrains runs and agreement to integers >= 1, lint enforces both cross-field rules). E_MISSING_FIXTURES extends to graduation intent: a judgment criterion carrying a judgment object with an empty fixtures list is invalid - its fixtures are its calibration corpus (it-graduation), and a graduation bar with no anchors is bare assertion wearing a rubric.
title: Structural validation and scope enforcement (lint)

gherkin:
Given a spec in which two records share an id
When lint runs
Then the spec is rejected with E_DUPLICATE_ID naming the duplicated id

Given a criterion whose contractId is not declared in the preamble's contracts
When lint runs
Then the spec is rejected with E_UNDECLARED_CONTRACT naming the criterion

Given a behavioral criterion with a declared contractId and an empty fixtures list
When lint runs
Then the spec is rejected with E_MISSING_FIXTURES naming the criterion

Given a criterion whose judgment object carries tolerance with 2 x agreement <= runs, or with agreement > runs
When lint runs
Then the spec is rejected with E_BAD_TOLERANCE naming the criterion

Given a judgment criterion carrying a judgment object and an empty fixtures list
When lint runs
Then the spec is rejected with E_MISSING_FIXTURES naming the criterion

Given a preamble whose roster carries the repo-owner role on more than one entry
When lint runs
Then the spec is rejected with E_MULTIPLE_OWNERS (ref preamble)
And given a preamble whose roster contains two entries with the same name, the spec is rejected with E_DUPLICATE_IMPLEMENTER naming the duplicated name

Given criterion records in state descriptive carrying source discovered and source forethought
When lint validates the spec
Then it is accepted - the state field admits descriptive, orthogonal to source
And a criterion whose state is outside the lifecycle enum is rejected with E_SCHEMA naming it - the enum stays closed

body:
A criterion gates conformance only if all hold: force MUST, contractId set to a contract declared in the preamble, state active or disputed - a disputed criterion continues to gate every implementer except the disputer - and either class behavioral, or class judgment carrying a judgment object: a graduatable criterion (it-graduation). (Derived resolution: design v1.1 lists 'state: active' in the gating conjunction while also requiring disputed criteria to keep gating non-disputers; this spec resolves the contradiction by admitting both states and excluding the disputer.) Gate is a subset of the allowlist: a criterion about an undeclared surface cannot gate no matter how it is written.

States: proposed (exists in committed interchange, never gates; excavate's output state), active, deprecated (retired from gating, kept for history), disputed (gates everyone except the disputing implementer; reported loudly everywhere), and descriptive (recorded as true but deliberately not law: it never gates, renders for every audience with its state field retained so it is never shown as ratified, and is terminal). A disputed criterion carries dispute: {by, reason, at} - 'by' is the implementer roster name whose reports stop gating on it (derived: the design names no schema home for dispute attribution).

The descriptive state (4.0.0) is the resting place for an observation that documents without legislating - honest archaeology (excavate) and known-but-ungated truths (authoring) both legitimately produce criteria that record how a system behaves while deliberately declining to make that behavior a MUST. An active MUST may also be demoted to descriptive by an ordinary committed edit - a MAJOR change (ac-vers-major) that strips it from gating exactly as deprecation does, distinct from the inert proposed<->descriptive re-designation; descriptive is terminal with respect to promotion (active is reached only by promoting a proposed criterion, never out of descriptive), not a bar on arriving there by demotion. Before 4.0.0 proposed carried both meanings - a candidate awaiting ratification AND a deliberate non-law - and a reader could not tell them apart; descriptive separates them. It never gates (it-gating's conjunction admits only active or disputed), it renders for every audience (non-deprecated) with its state field retained - so a non-active criterion is never presented as ratified, the render-side analog of refusing to assert bare conformance - and it is terminal: active is reachable only by ratifying a proposed criterion through the promotion protocol, never from descriptive, so promotion refuses a descriptive target exactly as it refuses any non-proposed one (E_NOT_PROPOSED). descriptive is reached by an ordinary committed edit, NOT a promotion transition - proposed and descriptive are both inert, gating no one, so re-designating one as the other changes no implementer's obligations and is not a ratification event (it-versioning); to revive a descriptive criterion as law an ordinary edit returns it to proposed and promotion ratifies it. State is orthogonal to source: a descriptive criterion may be discovered (excavate output, later designated) or forethought (authored as a known non-law). Excavate itself still emits only proposed (it-author-excavate X2) - it surfaces candidates, and designating one descriptive is a deliberate maintainer edit, never archaeology minting a terminal record.

Judgment-class criteria without a judgment object are advisory by construction - they appear in reports, never in the verdict, exactly as at 0.2.0. The judgment object is graduation intent: adding one to an active criterion changes every implementer's obligations (ac-vers-major's 'graduates a judgment criterion to gating' clause - MAJOR, a deliberate act, never an edit that slips through). A gating judgment criterion is satisfied iff the graduation function returns graduated for it over the verify input's judgmentRecords (D1J, it-graduation); unsatisfied it is waivable (D2) and otherwise drifts, exactly as a behavioral criterion with no passing record - gating that can be dodged by not submitting evidence is not gating. There is no judgment-specific verdict token: waivers already express sanctioned incompleteness, loudly, and a fourth token would weaken every existing report consumer. State transitions never re-judge: ratification and dispute change who gates, not what was judged - judgment evidence survives them by construction (the judgmentHash projection, it-judgment).
title: Gating and criterion states

gherkin:
Given a spec whose gating criteria all have passing records and a judgment MUST criterion without a judgment object under the same contract with a failing record
When verify derives the implementation's conformance
Then the verdict is conforms and the judgment result appears only in the report's advisory listing

Given a spec containing a proposed MUST criterion and a deprecated MUST criterion, neither with any passing record
When verify derives conformance
Then neither criterion gates and the verdict is conforms

Given a disputed gating criterion with failing records from the disputer and from another implementer
When verify reports each implementation
Then the disputer's verdict is conforms with the dispute reported loudly, and the other implementer's verdict is drifts at that criterion

item: When a dispute is resolved, the resolution shall carry acknowledgment from all roster implementers except the disputer, with a solo roster or deadlock tiebreaking to the repo owner, and an acknowledgment silent past the roster's declared timeout (default 30 days) shall record as lapsed rather than veto.

gherkin:
Given a spec with an active MUST judgment criterion carrying a judgment object and an adequate calibration corpus
When the implementation's judgment records graduate it, the verdict is conforms
And when they do not - insufficient evidence included - the criterion fails and the verdict is drifts, with an unexpired waiver yielding conforms-with-waivers and never bare conforms
And non-graduatable judgment criteria with records appear in the advisory listing - graduatable criteria, gating or not, never do
And a judgment record rejected by ingestJudgment anywhere in the verify input fails every graduation at G1 - criteria whose own records are pristine included, fail closed
And a disputed graduatable criterion gates everyone except the disputer, the dispute listed loudly, and the dispute itself stales no evidence

Given a spec carrying two descriptive MUST criteria - one source discovered with its provenance triplet, one source forethought - alongside a passing active criterion, none of the descriptive criteria carrying any record
When verify derives conformance
Then no descriptive criterion gates and the verdict is conforms, exactly as proposed and deprecated never gate (ac-gate-nonactive)
And the descriptive state composes with either source - state is orthogonal to provenance

body: Fixtures are the interop proof: Gherkin and EARS sentences carry human intent, canonical fixtures carry the contract. A fixture is {id, contractId?, description, input, expected, format}; input and expected are concrete JSON values and format names how to interpret them. contractId is optional since 0.2.0 (relaxing a 0.1.0 compilation fiat): when present it MUST name a contract declared in the preamble (lint: E_UNDECLARED_CONTRACT); a fixture without contractId carries no gating surface and exists so that advisory (contract-less) criteria can reference fixtures voluntarily — referencing a fixture never makes an advisory criterion gate. Two implementations interoperate when both pass the shared fixture corpus. Any behavioral criterion with a contractId MUST reference at least one fixture (lint: E_MISSING_FIXTURES); so MUST any judgment criterion carrying a judgment object - its fixtures are its calibration corpus (it-graduation). Judgment criteria without a judgment object are exempt and never gate. fixtureHash values in VerificationRecords use CS9, so staleness of a record against an edited fixture is mechanically detectable.
title: Fixtures and hashing

gherkin:
Given a fixture record
When a conforming implementation computes its canonical hash
Then the result is 'sha256:' plus the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes of the fixture's canonical record line excluding the trailing LF

body:
verify is a ledger, not a runner: checks run outside felag by whatever runner the implementation's Binding names; the runner submits VerificationRecords. A record is {criterionId, fixtureId?, fixtureHash?, implementation, implementationVersion, conformanceVersion, verdict: pass|fail|unverifiable, evidence, runner, at, attribution}; all fields except fixtureId and fixtureHash are required (derived: the design marks only those two optional). Records are self-reported; their check is reproducibility against the public fixture corpus, not identity. Ingest result format (derived): {"accepted": boolean, "errors": [code]} with codes sorted ascending; codes at 1.0.0: E_MISSING_FIELD, E_BAD_VERDICT, E_SCHEMA.

Verdict derivation (derived; the design gives the verdict tokens and waiver semantics but not the algorithm). Inputs: the spec's records, an implementation name, its VerificationRecords, its waiver ledger, and an evaluation instant asOf (derived: waiver expiry makes verdicts time-dependent and the design names no evaluation clock). For fixture exchange this input is one JSON object {asOf, implementation, judgmentRecords, records, spec, waivers} where spec is the concatenated parsed records of spec.jsonl and fixtures.jsonl, and judgmentRecords (optional since 3.0.0, absent meaning empty) is the JudgmentRecord evidence for graduatable judgment criteria (it-judgment, it-graduation).
Timestamps. Every timestamp in this contract - a record's at, a waiver's expiresAt, asOf - is an RFC 3339 date-time, and every comparison between timestamps is an instant comparison after UTC normalization, never lexical string order: lexical order diverges from instant order for non-Z offsets and for differing sub-second precision, and equal instants are ties. Parseable means exactly: RFC 3339 date-time with the T and Z designators case-insensitive (per its ABNF), a numeric offset or Z REQUIRED (a missing offset is not RFC 3339; a parser that reads it as host-local time makes the verdict depend on the box's timezone), and second 60 excluded - a leap second has no instant on the POSIX scale this contract normalizes to, so it is unparseable here, not mapped. Comparison resolution is the millisecond: a sub-millisecond fraction is truncated (not rounded), so two timestamps differing only below the millisecond are the same instant on every host. The date-time must also name a real calendar instant - month 01-12, day-of-month valid for that month and year (leap years included), hour 00-23, minute 00-59 - so an in-shape-but-impossible date (2026-02-30, hour 24) is unparseable, never deferred to a host parser whose out-of-range rollover is engine-defined. ingest rejects a record whose at does not parse (E_SCHEMA); a record reaching D1 with an unparseable at is ignored, like a stale one. asOf is the caller's evaluation instant; well-formedness is the caller's precondition (the promotion protocol, which has an error channel, instead G1-rejects unparseable timestamps). D1 deliberately has no asOf upper bound - a future-dated record still wins, because the ledger reports what was submitted; promotion bounds at <= asOf because acknowledgments are endorsements inside a deliberation window. The asymmetry is intended.
D1. A gating behavioral criterion (see it-gating) is satisfied if for every fixture it references, the latest record by 'at' (instant order; equal instants tie to the greatest array index - last submitted) matching (criterionId, fixtureId, implementation, conformanceVersion) has verdict pass; a record whose fixtureHash is present and differs from the referenced fixture's current canonical hash is stale and ignored.
D1J (3.0.0). A gating judgment criterion (it-gating: graduatable, state active or disputed) is satisfied iff graduate({criterionId, implementation, records: the input's FULL judgmentRecords array, spec}) returns graduated (it-graduation). verify never pre-validates judgmentRecords against the wire schema - verify is total with no error channel, its preconditions are the caller's, exactly as for D1's records; the fail-closed path is graduate's G1, which validates the full array for every graduation: a record ingestJudgment rejects - whatever criterion it names - fails every gating judgment criterion in the spec, criteria whose own records are pristine included. Records rejected by ingestJudgment never reach a ledger; an input carrying one is corrupt evidence, loud everywhere, never filtered quietly. D2 and D3 apply to judgment criteria unchanged.
D2. An unsatisfied gating criterion with an unexpired waiver (waiver.expiresAt > asOf as instants, matching criterionId and implementation, kind waiver or known-bug) is waived; an expired waiver is a failure again and is not listed as waived. A waiver whose expiresAt does not parse is expired - fail closed, a malformed waiver waives nothing. The fail-closed treatment is end-to-end: promotion refuses to mint a known-bug waiver whose expiresAt does not parse (G1, E_SCHEMA; fixture fx-promo-knownbug-badexpiry) and verify refuses to honor one that reaches the ledger by any other path (D2; fixture fx-instant-waiver-badstamp) - no seam admits a malformed-expiresAt waiver.
D3. Verdict: drifts if any gating criterion is neither satisfied nor waived; otherwise conforms-with-waivers if any criterion is waived; otherwise conforms. An implementation with active waivers never reports bare conforms.
D4. The report lists failing, waived, and disputed criterion ids (disputed criteria are listed for every implementation - loud everywhere) and an advisory listing of NON-GRADUATABLE judgment criteria - those without a judgment object - that have records, with their latest verdicts; advisory verdicts are VerificationRecord-borne self-reports. Graduatable judgment criteria never appear in advisory: when they gate they appear in failing or waived like every other gating criterion, and when they do not gate (proposed, deprecated, or descriptive state, or disputed for the disputer) their judgment evidence does not bear on this report at all - the graduation result is its own diagnostic surface.
D5. Report format (derived): {advisory: [{criterionId, verdict}], conformanceVersion, disputed: [id], failing: [id], implementation, verdict: conforms|conforms-with-waivers|drifts, waived: [id]}; id lists sorted ascending.
D6. Waivers are per-implementation and live in the implementation's ledger, not the spec repo: {criterionId, implementation, kind: waiver|known-bug, justification, attribution, expiresAt}.
title: VerificationRecord ingestion and verdict derivation

gherkin:
Given a VerificationRecord with all required fields and a valid verdict
When verify ingests it
Then the record is accepted

Given a VerificationRecord missing a required field and carrying a verdict outside pass|fail|unverifiable
When verify ingests it
Then the record is rejected with the error codes naming both defects

Given a spec and an implementation's records
When every gating criterion has passing records, the verdict is conforms
And when any gating criterion lacks a passing record, the verdict is drifts and the report names the failing criteria

Given a failing gating criterion covered by a waiver in the implementation's ledger
When the waiver is unexpired at asOf, the verdict is conforms-with-waivers, never bare conforms, and the report lists the waived criterion
And when the waiver is expired at asOf, the criterion fails again and the verdict is drifts

item: While deriving or reporting conformance, a felag/verifier implementation shall never execute the implementation under verification, spawn agents, or manage sessions; checks run outside felag and reach it only as VerificationRecords.

While processing attribution fields (discoveredBy, verdict provenance, waiver authors, record attribution), an implementation shall treat them as free-form strings with no semantics and shall not build behavior on their values.

gherkin:
Given VerificationRecords and waivers whose timestamps carry non-Z offsets, differing sub-second precision, lowercase designators, missing offsets, leap seconds, or garbage
When the ledger ingests records, selects D1's latest, and tests waiver expiry
Then every comparison is an instant comparison after UTC normalization - a lexically greater but instant-earlier timestamp never wins, equal instants tie to the greatest array index - unparseable ats fail ingest (E_SCHEMA) and are ignored at D1, and an unparseable waiver expiresAt is expired, fail closed

body:
Judgment verification applies the verify stance to judgment: felag never runs the judge - judges run outside the boundary, by whatever harness the implementation chooses, and their verdicts arrive as JudgmentRecords exactly as conformance checks arrive as VerificationRecords. A JudgmentRecord is {criterionId, judgmentHash, kind: calibration|target, fixtureId?, fixtureHash?, implementation?, conformanceVersion?, judge, verdict: pass|fail|unverifiable, evidence, runner, at, attribution}. One asymmetry stated plainly: a target verdict is attested evidence, weaker than a behavioral VerificationRecord. A behavioral record's check is reproducibility against the public fixture corpus - anyone can re-run the fixture and check the verdict. A target JudgmentRecord judges conduct that is in no corpus: only the judge's calibration is third-party-checkable; the target verdict is reproducible only by whoever can observe the conduct. Judgment gating is therefore calibrated attestation, and ratifying graduation intent accepts that bar - the runner-integrity trust model, applied to a sparser evidence stream.

judgmentHash - required on BOTH kinds - binds a record to the judgment projection: 'sha256:' followed by the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes of the canonical serialization (CS2, CS4, CS5) of the object {criterionId, rubric, text}, where criterionId is the criterion's id, rubric is its judgment.rubric, and text is its gherkin if type scenario, else its item. The projection is exactly what the judge was shown to judge against: the obligation text and the rubric. A record whose judgmentHash differs from the criterion's current projection hash is stale and ignored by graduation - amending the rubric or the criterion text resets the evidence loudly, never silently (the staleness mechanic of fixtureHash and the promotion ack's criterionHash, reused). Deliberately NOT in the projection: state and dispute (ratifying graduation intent must not void the evidence that justified ratifying it, and a third party's dispute must not stale a non-disputer's records - governance transitions change who gates, not what was judged), tolerance (an aggregation parameter re-evaluated on every graduation, not something the judge saw), fixtures (anchors bind per-anchor through fixtureHash, and admissibility is recomputed against the current corpus on every graduation), and the provenance fields. This is deliberately narrower than the promotion ack's criterionHash, which binds the full canonical line: an ack endorses the whole record once; judgment evidence accumulates across governance transitions.

kind calibration requires fixtureId and fixtureHash and forbids implementation and conformanceVersion: calibration is a property of the judge, not of anyone's conduct. kind target requires implementation and conformanceVersion and forbids fixtureId and fixtureHash: the judge was shown the implementation's actual conduct, not an anchor. fixtureHash is required on calibration records - stricter than VerificationRecord, where it is optional - because a calibration record's entire meaning is 'this judge reproduces the known verdict on exactly this anchor'; an unbound calibration is meaningless, and an edited anchor must recalibrate every judge, fail closed.

judge is {model}: structured matching plumbing, NOT attribution - the second kind of name in it-governance's two-kinds-of-names doctrine. Judge identity is the canonical serialization (CS2, CS4, CS5) of the judge object, compared for byte equality only: the graduation function groups records by it and builds no other behavior on its value - never parsed, never ranked, no version arithmetic. Publishers encode model, version, and configuration in the model string; felag compares bytes. ac-ver-attribution-opaque continues to govern the free-form attribution field, which judgment records also carry. A pinned judge-configuration field was deliberately rejected: a spec that names admissible judges hard-depends on models (vendor-neutrality applied to judging itself) and dies with every deprecation; the calibration corpus replaces it - any judge that reproduces the known verdicts is admissible (it-graduation).

ingestJudgment reuses the ingest result format {accepted, errors:[code]} and its codes: E_MISSING_FIELD (a field required for the record's kind is absent), E_SCHEMA (wrong types, kind-forbidden fields present, a judgmentHash or fixtureHash that is not 'sha256:' plus 64 lowercase hex, a malformed judge object, an at that does not parse per it-verification's instants rule - the schema's date-time format is annotation, not assertion; parseability is this prose rule, fixture-pinned), E_BAD_VERDICT (verdict outside pass|fail|unverifiable); errors sorted ascending.
title: Judgment records

gherkin:
Given JudgmentRecords of kind calibration and kind target carrying all kind-required fields
When ingestJudgment validates each, both are accepted
And a record missing judgmentHash, with a verdict outside pass|fail|unverifiable and a judge object carrying keys beyond model, is rejected naming all three defects
And a calibration record carrying implementation or conformanceVersion, or a target record carrying fixtureId or fixtureHash, is rejected with E_SCHEMA alongside E_MISSING_FIELD for its absent kind-required fields
And a judgmentHash that is not sha256: plus 64 lowercase hex is rejected with E_SCHEMA
And the projection draws its text from the gherkin of a scenario criterion, never its absent item

body:
Graduation is how a judgment criterion becomes gateable without felag ever judging: a total, deterministic, fixturable function of exactly (criterionId, implementation, records, spec) - the shape of promote and verify. The non-determinism (the judge model call) lives entirely in record production, outside the boundary; fixtures prove the function with synthetic judgment records, no live judge required.

A criterion is graduatable iff it carries a judgment object {rubric, tolerance?} with tolerance {runs, agreement} defaulting to {runs: 3, agreement: 3} - the default is pinned in this wire format, not in any spec record (the criteriaPerItem pattern). Unanimity-of-3 as the default is deliberate: disagreement at n=3 means the rubric is ambiguous, and an ambiguous rubric should not gate; authors relax it deliberately. Lint enforces 2 x agreement > runs (E_BAD_TOLERANCE), so reproducible-pass and reproducible-fail are mutually exclusive by construction. A graduatable criterion's fixtures list IS its calibration corpus: anchor fixtures, format felag/judgment-anchor@0, input the artifact to judge (payload-opaque, whatever the rubric needs), expected exactly {"verdict":"pass"} or {"verdict":"fail"} - one key, those values. Anchor adequacy lives here, not in lint: lint never reads payloads (an interchange invariant), while interpreting payloads per format is what payload-consuming functions are for. An anchor's format string is conventional documentation, not consulted by adequacy - the expected shape is the test. Anchor quality - are the anchors discriminating? - is the spec author's judgment conduct, ac-author-conduct's jurisdiction, the same place rubric quality lives.

Wire formats felag/graduation-input@0 {criterionId, implementation, records, spec} and felag/graduation-result@0 {graduated, errors, basis, judges, window} (see schema). Guards, mirroring promotion - each returns the full result with the single guard code, basis null, judges and window empty, and stops: G1 the input fails the wire-format schema, every record acceptable to ingestJudgment and timestamps parseable per it-verification's instants rule (E_SCHEMA); G2 spec fails lint (E_SPEC_INVALID); G3 criterionId names no criterion record (E_UNKNOWN_CRITERION); G4 the named criterion carries no judgment object (E_NOT_GRADUATABLE).

Definitions. Judge identity: the canonical serialization (CS2, CS4, CS5) of a record's judge object; equality is byte equality. Adequate corpus: the criterion's fixtures list is non-empty, every referenced anchor's expected parses as exactly {"verdict":"pass"} or {"verdict":"fail"}, and at least one anchor expects pass and at least one expects fail. The fail anchor is load-bearing: it is what kills the lazy always-pass judge, and it is why the agreement statistic needs no chance correction (a chance-corrected coefficient was rejected: floating-point statistics break fixture byte-equality across languages, and kappa is undefined at exactly the perfect agreement the protocol rewards). Admissible judge: judge J is admissible for criterion C iff C's corpus is adequate and for EVERY anchor in C.fixtures, the latest calibration record by J for (C.id, anchor id) whose judgmentHash equals C's current projection hash (it-judgment) and whose fixtureHash equals the anchor's current canonical hash - instant order on at, equal instants tying to the greatest array index, D1's rule verbatim - exists and has verdict equal to the anchor's expected verdict. The bar is all anchors, exactly: the corpus is author-curated to be unambiguous, and a judge wrong on an unambiguous anchor is inadmissible (a pass-rate knob, if real corpora ever need one, is a MINOR addition). Qualifying record: a target record matching criterionId = C.id, the input's implementation, and conformanceVersion equal to the spec preamble's, whose judgmentHash equals C's current projection hash, whose at parses, and whose judge is admissible. Window: the latest tolerance.runs qualifying records by instant, equal instants tying to the greatest array index. Independence of runs is attested, not verified: records are self-reported, and their check is calibration against the public anchor corpus, not identity - the runner-integrity stance; a distinctJudges floor is deliberately deferred (MINOR-addable, tightening only criteria that opt in).

Derivation, basis precedence (first that holds): corpus-inadequate; no-admissible-judge (adequate corpus, zero admissible judges among the input's records for C - an input with no records at all included); insufficient-evidence (fewer than tolerance.runs qualifying records); then over the full window, counting passes p and fails f - unverifiable occupies its slot and counts toward neither (an abstention is evidence of non-reproducibility; fail closed, the malformed-waiver stance): satisfied iff p >= agreement, reproducible-fail iff f >= agreement (the judges agree the conduct violates - a conduct problem), else unreproducible (the judges split - a rubric problem; the basis names the remedy). graduated is true iff basis is satisfied.

Provenance is derived and loud, never carried: the result's judges lists every distinct judge identity appearing in the input's records for C - calibration or target - as {admissible, judge}, sorted ascending by the Unicode code points of the judge identity's canonical serialization (CS4's order, never UTF-16 code-unit order); window lists the selected target records as {at, judge, verdict} in selection order (instant ascending, ties by array index), each at exactly as carried on the record, never normalized. The result's window is empty for every basis except satisfied, reproducible-fail, and unreproducible - the early bases select no window even when some records qualify. Records carry only binding-shaped provenance (judge identity, judgmentHash, fixtureHash); reproducibility stats and calibration evidence are recomputed from the ledger every time, the same reason promote recomputes effective decisions rather than trusting a tally field.

Graduation is state-independent: it evaluates a proposed criterion identically to an active one - you test graduation before ratifying graduation intent, and the evidence survives ratification (the projection excludes state; it-judgment). Whether the result gates anyone is it-gating's business; whether to ratify the intent is the promotion protocol's.
title: The graduation function

gherkin:
Given a graduation input missing a required field or carrying a record ingestJudgment rejects, the result is E_SCHEMA alone
And given a spec that fails lint, the result is E_SPEC_INVALID alone
And given a criterionId naming no criterion, the result is E_UNKNOWN_CRITERION alone
And given a criterion without a judgment object, the result is E_NOT_GRADUATABLE alone
And a proposed criterion graduates identically to an active one - graduation is state-independent

Given a judgment criterion whose corpus carries pass and fail anchors
When a judge's latest calibration records bound to the current projection and anchor hashes match every anchor's expected verdict, the judge is admissible - a later correct calibration supersedes an earlier wrong one
And when a judge fails any anchor or its only calibration is stale against the current hashes, the judge is inadmissible and its target records never qualify
And when the corpus lacks a pass or fail anchor or any expected does not parse as a verdict, the basis is corpus-inadequate for every judge
And with an adequate corpus and zero admissible judges among the input's records - an input with no records at all included - the basis is no-admissible-judge
And the result's judges list orders identities ascending by the Unicode code points of their canonical serialization

Given qualifying target records from admissible judges
When the window is selected, it is the latest tolerance.runs records by instant after UTC normalization - a lexically greater but instant-earlier at never wins, equal instants tie to the greatest array index - and records with a stale judgmentHash, a conformanceVersion differing from the preamble's, or another implementation's name never enter
And when fewer than tolerance.runs records qualify, the basis is insufficient-evidence and the result's window is empty

Given a full window of verdicts from admissible judges
When passes reach agreement, the basis is satisfied and graduated is true
And when fails reach agreement, the basis is reproducible-fail
And when neither side reaches agreement - unverifiable verdicts occupying their slots and counting toward neither - the basis is unreproducible
And when the criterion's judgment object omits tolerance, the pinned default runs 3 agreement 3 applies

body: conformanceVersion is semver. Fixtures carry the contract, so editing one is a behavior change wearing a test's clothes. These rules are stated as obligations on spec changes; at 1.0.0 no verb is contractually obligated to enforce them mechanically (lint's version-bump consistency check is named in the design but its inputs are unspecified), so the criteria below are advisory. State distinction (1.0.0): criteria in state proposed are inert - they gate no one - so their addition and their text edits are MINOR; the moment gating obligations change is ratification. The normative-text rule (1.0.0) reaches item bodies: algorithm and rule text carried in bodies (CS1-CS9, D1-D6, the promotion guards and predicates) is as normative as criterion text, and material changes to it are MAJOR; pure clarification prose remains PATCH. The MUST/PATCH line is whether any conforming implementation's obligations change.
title: Versioning

item: When a change adds a MUST criterion in state active, modifies an existing fixture's input or expected, removes a fixture, graduates a judgment criterion to gating, deprecates an active MUST criterion, demotes an active MUST criterion to descriptive (it strips an active MUST from gating exactly as deprecation does), ratifies a proposed MUST criterion to active, or materially changes normative text (the gherkin or item of an active MUST criterion, an active MUST judgment criterion's rubric or tolerance, or algorithm/rule text carried in an item body), the spec shall increment the MAJOR component of conformanceVersion.

When a change adds a SHOULD or MAY criterion, adds any criterion in state proposed, edits a proposed criterion's text, ratifies a proposed SHOULD or MAY criterion, adds a new fixture to an existing criterion, or deprecates a SHOULD or MAY criterion, the spec shall increment MINOR; when a change is limited to clarifications, prose, renders, or fixture description and metadata, the spec shall increment PATCH.

body: A reimplementation targets classes, not the whole surface. Class to verb and contract mapping at 1.0.0: felag/interchange covers lint and validates the interchange format itself, Profile and Binding artifact formats, canonical serialization, and index rebuild - its gating surface is contract c-interchange. felag/verifier covers verify, audit, and (3.0.0) graduate, and validates VerificationRecord and JudgmentRecord ingestion, the graduation function, waivers, reports, and coverage - its gating surface is contract c-verification. felag/author covers author, excavate, render, and prime - its contract is c-author (items it-author-interview, it-author-excavate, it-author-render, it-author-promotion), whose criteria are state proposed at 1.0.0: published, fixtured, reviewable, gating no one until ratified through the promotion protocol itself. The class remains partially judgment-verified: interview conduct and stakeholder-render language are judgment; every verb's output is behavioral. audit's task-proposal idempotency on (specItemRef, criterionId) belongs to the felag-tasks sibling contract and is not specified here.
title: Conformance classes

item: When an implementation claims felag conformance, it shall declare the conformance class or classes it targets (felag/interchange, felag/verifier, felag/author), and its gating obligations shall be exactly the gating criteria of the contracts mapped to those classes.
When a felag/author implementation produces a conformance report, the report shall state on its face that author-class conformance is partially judgment-verified.

While defining or deriving conformance, an implementation shall depend on no model, vendor, or agent framework; the no-LLM authoring path (hand-written interchange lines validated by lint) shall remain sufficient, and prime shall emit vendor-neutral markdown.

body:
Two kinds of names exist and they are different kinds of things. Attribution fields (discoveredBy, verdict provenance, waiver authors, record attribution) are free-form strings with no semantics - ac-ver-attribution-opaque stands. Roster entries (the preamble's implementers: names and roles) are governance plumbing and DO carry semantics where the contract reads them: dispute.by names whose reports a disputed criterion stops gating (it-gating), acknowledgments and requestedBy in promotion inputs are roster references, and the role string 'repo-owner' mechanically resolves promotion deadlocks (it-author-promotion). The roster's declared timeout is the preamble's governance.timeoutDays (default 30 when absent) - where prose elsewhere says 'the roster's declared timeout', it means this field.

Because 'repo-owner' is mechanically load-bearing, role edits are governance acts, explicitly overriding the rule that roster membership changes by ordinary spec PR for this one case: adding, removing, or moving the repo-owner role requires ratification-grade acknowledgment from all roster implementers EXCEPT the entry whose role changes; that entry's nak records loudly but does not veto (the owner cannot entrench themselves against demotion). Solo roster: degenerate, the owner edits freely. This rule is social, merge-gated governance - reviewed by humans on the PR, not computed by a function; mechanizing it (a role-edit transition variant) is named future work. Plain membership changes remain ordinary PRs.
title: Roster semantics and governance

item: When a spec change adds, removes, or moves the repo-owner role on the implementers roster, the change shall carry acknowledgment from all roster implementers except the entry whose role changes, the affected entry's objection shall be recorded loudly without vetoing, and a solo roster shall degenerate to the owner editing freely.

body:
The interview is conduct: greenfield, delta, and (deferred) --from-annotations flows; the front-loaded questions ('contract or choice? could a stranger get it wrong? which fixture proves it?'); the preference for fixtures over checklists. Conduct is judgment - felag never runs the interview and cannot fixture a dialog. What gates is the interview's OUTPUT.

Wire format felag/author-output@0: {spec, new, budgets?} where spec is the complete post-interview record set, new lists the criterion ids this interview authored, and budgets defaults to {criteriaPerItem: 7} when absent - the default is pinned in this wire format, not in any spec record. Result: lint-shaped {valid, errors:[{code, ref}]}, errors sorted ascending by (code, ref), codes the union of lint codes and E_BUDGET_CRITERIA, E_BAD_PROVENANCE, E_UNKNOWN_CRITERION.

A1: the emitted record set passes lint - an author implementation that emits unlintable interchange does not conform. A2: no item may carry more criteria than the effective criteriaPerItem (E_BUDGET_CRITERIA naming the item) - the cap is the protocol's defense against Cucumber-style sprawl, so the cap itself is mechanical. A3: every criterion listed in new carries source forethought ('discovered' is excavate's word; an author implementation emitting it for interview output is lying about provenance) - violations E_BAD_PROVENANCE naming the criterion, a new id naming no criterion E_UNKNOWN_CRITERION. Carried-through records keep their existing provenance; A3 binds only newly-authored work. The no-LLM path is normative and already covered: hand-written interchange validated by lint IS an author-output passing A1-A3.
title: The interview protocol (author)

gherkin:
Given an author-output whose spec passes lint and whose new criteria carry forethought provenance
When the output is validated, it is accepted
And when the spec fails lint, the lint error codes appear in the result

Given an author-output whose budgets set criteriaPerItem and an item carrying more criteria than the cap
When the output is validated
Then it is rejected with E_BUDGET_CRITERIA naming the item

Given an author-output listing a criterion in new
When that criterion carries source discovered, validation rejects with E_BAD_PROVENANCE naming it
And when the new id names no criterion in spec, validation rejects with E_UNKNOWN_CRITERION naming the id

item: While conducting an authoring interview, an implementation shall front-load the questions 'contract or choice?', 'could a stranger get it wrong?', and 'which fixture proves it?', shall prefer fixtures over checklists for anything contractual, and shall respect declared scenario budgets.

body:
Excavate reads a repo - outside felag's verifiable boundary, the same stance as verify: felag checks artifacts, not the archaeology. Wire format felag/excavate-output@0: {scope, spec} where scope is {contracts:[id]} and required non-empty. Result: lint-shaped, codes the union of lint codes and E_NO_SCOPE, E_BAD_PROVENANCE, E_OUT_OF_SCOPE.

X1: scope is required and scope.contracts non-empty, else E_NO_SCOPE (ref 'scope') - unbounded excavation is how you mirror a whole repo into a junk-drawer spec. X1 is a structural guard, mirroring the promotion guards: an absent or empty scope returns E_NO_SCOPE alone, with X2 and X3 unevaluated - an empty scope makes X3 ill-posed (out of WHAT scope?), the same reason promotion refuses at G2 rather than guessing. X2: every emitted criterion is source discovered and state proposed, carrying discoveredAt, discoveredBy, triggeringEvent, evidence (where the behavior and its expecteds were read), and - when it carries no fixture - unfixturable naming why it cannot be carried by a fixture in the chosen projection (a criterion declaring unfixturable is exempt from E_MISSING_FIXTURES) - violations E_BAD_PROVENANCE naming the criterion. Excavate output never gates anyone; only the promotion protocol can activate it. X3: the emitted record set passes lint, and criteria reference only contracts named in scope.contracts (E_OUT_OF_SCOPE otherwise).

Projection (6.0.0): a discovered fixture whose format MODELS a non-deterministic or excluded impl - rather than being the impl native wire format - declares projection, a string naming the model. felag checks well-formedness only and surfaces declared projections to the verifier audience (renderInventory.projections), so the reviewer audits projection fidelity as a bounded list; it cannot detect an UNdeclared projection - that is outside the boundary, and felag does not pretend otherwise. The honesty boundary, stated plainly: felag checks the PRESENCE of evidence, unfixturable, and projection - never their TRUTH. Whether a discovered expected matches the cited code, or a projection is faithful, rests entirely on the cold-review and promotion layer; felag reads no repo and runs no impl. evidence and projection turn that human audit into a checklist instead of a re-derivation.
title: The excavate output contract

gherkin:
Given an excavate-output without a scope, validation rejects with E_NO_SCOPE
And given a scoped output whose criteria are discovered, proposed, and provenance-complete
Then validation accepts it

Given an excavate-output containing a criterion that is not source discovered, not state proposed, or missing discoveredAt, discoveredBy, or triggeringEvent
When the output is validated
Then it is rejected with E_BAD_PROVENANCE naming the criterion

Given an excavate-output whose scope names some contracts and a criterion referencing a declared contract outside that scope
When the output is validated
Then it is rejected with E_OUT_OF_SCOPE naming the criterion

Given an excavate-output whose discovered criterion carries full discovered/proposed provenance but no evidence reference
When the output is validated
Then it is rejected with E_BAD_PROVENANCE naming the criterion - evidence (where the behavior and its expecteds were read) is required so cold-review checks the cited source rather than re-deriving the truth

Given two fixtureless discovered criteria, one naming why it is unfixturable in the chosen projection and one carrying no fixtures and no reason
When the output is validated
Then the one declaring unfixturable is accepted and exempt from E_MISSING_FIXTURES, and the silent one is rejected with E_BAD_PROVENANCE - degradation to prose must be named

Given an excavate-output whose discovered fixture declares a projection, and the verifier render of a spec carrying that fixture
When the output is validated and the spec rendered
Then the projection-declaring fixture is accepted (a format may model the impl rather than be its wire format) and the verifier inventory surfaces it in projections so the reviewer audits projection fidelity

body:
Render aesthetics are excluded surface ('observable but undeclared, therefore non-core'); what is contractual is audience projection - WHAT each audience sees, never how it is typeset. Wire format felag/render-inventory@0: {spec, audience: stakeholder|developer|verifier}. Result {included, excludedFields}: both EXACT sets, sorted ascending, equality-checked. included ranges over id-bearing records (items, criteria, fixtures); the preamble has no id and is included for every audience by definition.

Stakeholder: every item and every non-deprecated criterion; excludedFields exactly [class, contractId, discoveredAt, discoveredBy, fixtures, interfaceSketch, itemId, judgment, source, triggeringEvent, type] - machine plumbing and the provenance triplet. Retained: criterion text, force (MUST/SHOULD/MAY is stakeholder-meaningful), dispute, and state - criteria render with their state and non-active states are marked loudly; a proposed criterion rendered as if ratified is the render-side version of asserting bare conformance. Developer: every item, every non-deprecated criterion, every fixture; excludedFields []. The working view: full contract surface, no retired history. Verifier: the identity projection - every id-bearing record including deprecated criteria; excludedFields []. Renders are one-way artifacts: a render is never input to any felag verb except the future author --from-annotations; no verb in this contract accepts markdown (structurally enforced - no wire format has a markdown input). Stakeholder-render language quality stays judgment: fixturing prose style would pin aesthetics, which the exclusions forbid.
title: The render protocol

gherkin:
Given a spec and audience stakeholder
When the render inventory is derived
Then included is exactly every item and every non-deprecated criterion and excludedFields is exactly the eleven-field machine-plumbing list

Given a spec and audience developer
When the render inventory is derived
Then included is exactly every item, every non-deprecated criterion, and every fixture, with no excluded fields

Given a spec and audience verifier
When the render inventory is derived
Then included is exactly every id-bearing record including deprecated criteria, with no excluded fields

item: While producing a stakeholder render, an implementation shall use observable language free of implementation jargon, and shall mark non-active criterion states loudly.

body:
Ratification as a total, deterministic, fixturable function of exactly (spec, transition, asOf) - the fixable half of the F6 governance-enforceability gap. Wire formats felag/promotion-input@0 and felag/promotion-result@0 (see schema). Every acknowledgment carries criterionHash: the CS9 hash of the criterion's canonical record line AS ACKNOWLEDGED - acks are bound to the text they endorse, exactly as VerificationRecords carry fixtureHash.

Definitions. Valid acknowledgment: requestedAt <= at <= asOf, compared - like every timestamp comparison in this protocol - as instants after UTC normalization, never lexically (violation is loud: E_BAD_ACK). Stale acknowledgment: valid, but criterionHash differs from the target criterion's current canonical hash; stale acks are ignored for effective decisions and listed in the result's stale field - an amendment resets endorsement visibly, never silently. Effective decision per roster implementer: the latest valid, non-stale acknowledgment by at as an instant, equal instants broken by greatest array index (last submitted). Lapsed: no effective decision and asOf > requestedAt + timeoutDays, where + timeoutDays means timeoutDays x 86400 seconds added to the UTC-normalized requestedAt instant, compared as instants - never calendar arithmetic (a wall-clock reading diverges across a DST transition and flips the verdict at the lapse boundary). The repo owner: the unique roster entry whose roles include repo-owner; the owner's effective decision is three-valued (ack, nak, none), none when the unique owner has no effective decision and also when zero entries carry the role (no tiebreak available); the multiple-owner case never reaches the predicates - it fails lint (E_MULTIPLE_OWNERS) and stops at guard G2.

Evaluation. Three structural guards, each returning the full result object with the single guard code and stopping: G1 input fails the wire-format schema; every timestamp field - requestedAt, each acknowledgment's at, asOf, and a known-bug transition's expiresAt when present - must parse as an RFC 3339 date-time (parseable as defined in it-verification's Timestamps rule), else E_SCHEMA: an unparseable expiresAt slipping G1 would ratify a known-bug with a born-dead waiver; G2 spec is not lint-valid -> E_SPEC_INVALID (without lint-validity, 'the target criterion' and 'the roster entry named X' are not well-defined - unstated preconditions are the divergence class felag exists to eliminate; fixture inputs are adversarial and need not be committed specs); G3 criterionId names no criterion record -> E_UNKNOWN_CRITERION. Otherwise errors is the sorted set of every holding predicate - all-applicable, never short-circuiting, E_VETOED and E_PENDING co-fire when both hold:

E_NOT_PROPOSED: the target criterion's state is not proposed (promotion is not a cheaper deprecation or un-dispute). E_BAD_REQUEST: requestedAt > asOf as instants. E_NOT_ROSTER: requestedBy or any acknowledgment's implementer names no roster entry. E_BAD_ACK: any acknowledgment is invalid. E_MISSING_FIELD: to is known-bug and any of implementation, justification, expiresAt, attribution is absent. E_VETOED - for to active or known-bug: the owner's effective decision is nak, OR a non-owner's effective decision is nak and the owner's effective decision is nak or none (only an owner ack overrides; with no owner any nak stands); for to rejected: the owner's effective decision is nak. E_PENDING - for to active or known-bug: some roster implementer has neither an effective decision nor lapsed; for to rejected: no roster implementer's effective decision is ack.

accepted iff errors is empty; outcome is ratified for accepted active/known-bug, rejected for accepted rejected, else null; lapsed and stale list roster names sorted ascending - liveness and amendment-resets are loud, never silent. Rejection is deliberately lighter than ratification: one effective ack from any roster implementer and no owner nak - ratification creates obligations for every implementer, rejection deletes an inert proposal that never gated anyone (history lives in git, re-proposing is one PR). Solo roster degenerates explicitly to repo-owner authority: one valid ack ratifies. known-bug is a ratification plus a waiver built entirely from input fields: it presupposes triage amended the proposed criterion to state the CORRECT behavior (editing a proposed criterion is an ordinary PR - proposed is inert and criterionHash staleness makes the amendment loud); the bug never becomes a MUST, the correct behavior does, with the divergence tracked as a kind known-bug waiver in the named implementation's ledger. The function returns a verdict; applying the activation or deletion to the interchange files is the caller's write, same as verify reports without mutating the ledger.
title: The promotion protocol

gherkin:
Given a promotion input failing the wire-format schema, the result is E_SCHEMA alone
And given a transition over a spec that fails lint, the result is E_SPEC_INVALID alone
And given a criterionId naming no criterion, the result is E_UNKNOWN_CRITERION alone

Given a transition to active
When every roster implementer effectively acks or lapses past the committed timeout, the criterion ratifies and lapsed names are listed loudly
And when acknowledgments are neither complete nor lapsed, the result is E_PENDING
And when the target criterion is not proposed, the result includes E_NOT_PROPOSED

Given a non-owner nak
When the repo owner's effective decision is ack, the deadlock resolves and the transition ratifies with the nak recorded
And when the owner's effective decision is nak or none, the result includes E_VETOED
And E_VETOED and E_PENDING co-fire when both hold

Given multiple acknowledgments from one implementer, the latest valid non-stale by at wins, ties to the last submitted
And an acknowledgment outside the requestedAt..asOf window is E_BAD_ACK, loudly
And a valid acknowledgment whose criterionHash mismatches the current criterion is stale: ignored for decisions, listed in stale
And a request with requestedAt after asOf is E_BAD_REQUEST

Given a transition to rejected
When any roster implementer effectively acks and the owner does not nak, the proposal is rejected
And when no implementer acks, the result is E_PENDING

Given a transition to known-bug with implementation, justification, expiresAt, and attribution
When the ratification quorum holds, the outcome is ratified and the result carries a kind known-bug waiver built from those fields
And when any of the four fields is absent, the result includes E_MISSING_FIELD

Given transitions whose acknowledgment, requestedAt, asOf, or known-bug expiresAt timestamps carry non-Z offsets or do not parse
When validity windows, effective decisions, and E_BAD_REQUEST are evaluated
Then requestedAt <= at <= asOf, latest-by-at, and requestedAt > asOf are instant comparisons after UTC normalization, and any unparseable timestamp - expiresAt included - fails the wire format at G1 with E_SCHEMA

body: prime emits the protocols, vendor-neutral. Mechanical half: wire format felag/prime-output@0 {spec, output} - the emitted document must contain, verbatim (substring), the body of every PROTOCOL ITEM, where a protocol item is defined mechanically as an item with at least one criterion whose contractId is c-author (items carry no contract membership of their own; this derivation is computable from the records, and it-governance is deliberately NOT a protocol item - its judgment criterion carries no contractId, mirroring ac-gate-dispute-resolution: governance is for spec maintainers, not implementation protocol). Missing body -> E_MISSING_PROTOCOL naming the item; result is lint-shaped with that single code. Judgment half: vendor-neutrality of any added framing is already covered by ac-class-vendor-neutral; prime adds no new judgment surface.
title: Prime

gherkin:
Given a spec and an emitted prime document
When the document contains the body of every item owning at least one c-author criterion, validation accepts it
And when any protocol item's body is absent, validation rejects with E_MISSING_PROTOCOL naming the item
